Tuairisc Bhainistíochta Mhíosúil an Príomhfheidhmeannach – 30ú Meán Fomhair 2025 
Chief Executive’s Monthly Management Report – 30th September 2025 
 
 
 
A Chara, 
 
I enclose the above report for your statutory consideration, this report has also been prepared under Section 136 
& 138 of the Local Government Act, 2001. The attached report is the Chief Executive’s Monthly Management 
Report for September 2025, detailing activities, updates, and progress across various departments of Louth 
County Council.  
 
Key Achievements and Deliverables: 
1. Finance and System Support 
• 
Expenditure: €122.76M spent (67% of budget). Housing accounted for 73% of its budget. 
• 
Income: €120.89M received (66% invoiced). Rates collection exceeded budget at 106%. 
• 
Debtors: Closing balance of €48.63M, with €26.52M owed by government debtors. 
• 
ICT helpdesk looked after 1048 support calls logged in the IT support system. 89% of these calls have 
been completed. 
• 
The ICT Department delivers regular cybersecurity training to all staff across the organisation, in 
September the focus was on the risks associated with sharing personal or work-related information on 
social media, also in 14.4% of inbound e-mails were identified as potentially harmful. 
 
2. Economic Delivery 
• 
Tourism Strategy 2025-2031: Endorsed by the SPC and ready for member consideration. 
• 
Lú Festival of Light, which is being delivered in 2025 by Love Drogheda BIDS, takes place from Friday, 
24th to Monday, 27th October. Please visit www.lufestivaloflight.com for further information. 
• 
41 Business Advice Clinics were carried out in September alongside 5 financial business advice clinics.  
• 
Shopfront Improvement Grant Scheme: 59 applications received. 
• 
Drogheda Night-Time Economy: Successful events like Culture Night Late and Safe Gigs Ireland 
partnership. 
• 
Drogheda Digital Innovation Hub: Opened for public use, supporting start-ups and remote workers. 
 
3. Operations & Environment Delivery 
• 
 LCC’s VARCITIES project was the winner in the Smart Cities and Urban Development Category at the 
eGovernment Awards. 
• 
Extensive repairs, drainage works, and footpath upgrades across Louth continue. 
• 
Illegal Dumping, CCTV installed at 5 sites, reducing complaints. The Waste Enforcement team also 
participated in a multiagency day of action on the M1 this month. 
• 
Waste Management: 2,233 mattresses and 2,124 couches collected during amnesty events. 
• 
Climate Action: Solar PV installations underway at 21 public buildings; 57% energy efficiency 
improvement achieved. 
• 
LCC has achieved a 57% improvement in energy efficiency and a 41% reduction in carbon emissions 
from their respective baseline years, already achieved its 2030 target for energy efficiency and is on 
target to meet its 2030 energy emissions target. 
 
4. HR, Community & Corporate Services 
•

• 
Community Climate Action Fund: 22 projects supported; second round of applications expected in 
Autumn. 
• 
Age-Friendly Initiatives: Workshops and events held to promote inclusivity for older adults. 
• 
Schools Programme: Progress on Ardee Educate Together National School nearing completion. 
• 
Sports Initiatives: New walking groups launched; inclusive hockey program started. 
 
5. Housing & Culture Delivery 
• 
Homelessness: 161 adults and 24 families in emergency accommodation; 54 Housing First tenancies 
established. 
• 
Housing Allocations: 60 units allocated (14 LA, 46 AHB). 
• 
Energy Efficiency Retrofits: 138 units targeted for upgrades in 2025. 
• 
Affordable Housing: 8 houses sold in Drogheda; 11 houses in Ardee open for applications. 
• 
Cultural Services: Libraries hosted events like Culture Night, Summer Stars, and Baby Book Club. 
Visitor numbers doubled at Dunleer Library. 
• 
Culture Night: Largest program yet, featuring performances, exhibitions, and workshops across Louth. 
• 
Creative Ireland: Supported projects like Encore Productions’ “Frankenstein.” 
• 
Museum: Hosted events like textile workshops, storytelling, and audio equipment exhibitions. 
 
6. Major Capital Projects & Infrastructure Delivery 
• 
Narrow Water Bridge: Construction progressing; bridge fabrication ongoing in Belgium. 
• 
Greenways: Carlingford Lough Greenway completed; celebration event held. 
• 
Town Centre First Plans: Draft plan for Clogherhead nearing completion; public square design 
underway in Dunleer. 
• 
Road Projects: N53 Hackballscross to Rassan tendering; PANCR Phase 2 works expected in January 
2026. 
 
This report highlights some of the Louth County Council's progress across the various directorates.  
I would like to take this opportunity to thanks all the executive and staff of LCC for their hard work and 
commitment, which is outlined in more detail in this report.

Cyber Security 
 
The ICT Department delivers regular cybersecurity training to all staff across the organisation. The focus of the 
September session was on the risks associated with sharing personal or work-related information on social 
media. Staff were informed that such disclosures can be exploited by cybercriminals to impersonate individuals 
or launch targeted scams. The training also reinforced the importance of reporting any suspicious activity to the 
IT Security Team promptly.

Drogheda Digital Innovation Hub 
 
 
Drogheda Digital Hub opens doors free to public ahead of 
launch 
 
Entrepreneurs, remote workers, and creatives in 
Drogheda are being invited to sample the town’s 
new Digital Hub with desks and meeting spaces 
available free of charge until 1st October.  The hub, 
located on Narrow West Street, is due to be officially 
opened next month, but the Council has announced 
a soft launch to give the public an early look. 
 
The Drogheda Digital Hub is designed to support 
start-ups, remote workers, and growing tech 
enterprises with affordable co-working spaces, 
meeting rooms, private booths, and breakout areas.  
With over twenty desks and a range of business 
support services - including training and tailored 
mentoring programmes - the Hub provides a 
modern, professional environment for entrepreneurs 
and creatives alike.  This is a key milestone in the 
urban renewal of West Street and support for the 
region’s next generation of businesses.
